chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Arqat, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not be a wanderer in the markets, nor manage the minute details of goods yourself, for it is not befitting for a Muslim man of noble lineage and religion to manage the purchase of minute goods himself, except for three things; for it is befitting for the one of religion and lineage to manage them himself: real estate, slaves, and camels.'

key_terms.دَوَّاراً: Wanderer / one who moves about frequently

ai.seo_question: What three items are appropriate for a nobleman to manage personally according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the etiquette of social hierarchy (*adab al-mansab*) by advising men of noble lineage (*dhawu al-husab*) to avoid the minutiae of daily retail trade, which was often associated with lower social strata. He explicitly exempts three major assets—real estate (*al-‘aqar*), slaves (*al-raqiqa*), and camels (*al-ibil*)—as these represented significant capital investments requiring direct oversight by the head of the household, thereby preserving their dignity while maintaining economic responsibility.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Amro Bin Ibrahim, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Haroun Bin Al Jaham, from Al Arqat who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do not become roamers in the markets, nor pursue the minute things by yourself, for it is no befitting for the Muslim man with esteem and the Religion that he buys the minute things by himself, except for three things which are befitting for the one with Religion and he esteem that he should puruse by himself – the real estate, and the slaves, and the camels’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from ‘Amr ibn Ibrahim from Khalaf ibn Hammad from Harun ibn al-Jahm from al-Arqat who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘You must not roam around in market places and you must not perform small tasks personally; it is not proper for a Muslim man of good position and religion to buy small things personally, except three kinds of items, in which case a person of good position and religion should personally perform, such as real estate, slaves and camels.’”
